title: Observation of Slow Magnetic Relaxation in Discrete Dysprosium Cubane

synthesis.procedure: The Schiff-base ligand was prepared by condensation of 2-hydrazinobenzothiazole (0.165 g, 1 mmol) with o-vanillin (0.1673 g, 1.1 mmol) in methanol (10 mL); 2-hydrazinobenzothiazole was obtained by a literature procedure. For complex 1, Dy(ClO4)3·6H2O (85.2 mg, 0.15 mmol) and the Schiff base (44.8 mg, 0.15 mmol) in 15 mL methanol/pyridine (2:1 v/v) were stirred for 4 h. Isonicotinic acid (18.4 mg, 0.15 mmol) was then added and the mixture was stirred for 1 h. The yellow solution was left undisturbed for slow solvent evaporation, giving yellow single crystals after 2 weeks. The Schiff base promotes crystallization but is not incorporated in the cubane.
synthesis.time: 4 h, then 1 h stirring; crystals after 2 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution stirring followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow solution left unperturbed; yellow single crystals formed by slow evaporation after 2 weeks.

properties.summary: Complex 1 is a discrete Dy4 cubane SMM. χMT falls from the uncoupled Dy(III) value on cooling because of Dy–Dy exchange and depopulation of Stark levels. Magnetization is unsaturated and below the free-ion limit because of anisotropy and crystal-field splitting. Frequency-dependent ac susceptibility shows slow relaxation below 6 K; above 3.1 K relaxation is thermally activated (U = 40.2 K, τ0 ≈ 1.1×10^-11 s), with a crossover toward a temperature-independent regime at lower temperature. A dc field does not effectively suppress possible zero-field quantum relaxation above 1.9 K.
